api.name: describe
api.summary: List the problems (presets) with their ids, dimensions, end times and parameters, and the fields, variables and choices a setup can make.

api.name: check
api.summary: Check a setup document before running it. Returns `ok`, an `error` if it cannot be read at all (with the key at fault), `notes` (keys dropped, values held to their range), and `issues`: each with a level (`error`: a rule broken, such as a star without isolated self-gravity, or a value that cannot work; `warning`: a choice to look at again, such as a softening under two cells, bodies that overlap or leave the box, a grid past the GPU memory), a sentence, and the path of the part or option it is about. Use it after writing or changing a document and before `load`.

api.name: meshFile
api.summary: Give the page a mesh file a setup document refers to (a `mesh` shape’s `file`: STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF, GLB, or an airfoil .dat or SVG outline), by that name, before `load`. Returns its size in bytes.

args.name: name
args.description: The name the setup gives the file

api.name: preset
api.summary: A preset’s whole setup document: a starting point for one of your own.

api.name: load
api.summary: Build a new run from a setup and leave it paused at t = 0. A setup is a preset with overrides, or a whole setup document (`document`) that assembles a run from parts: point masses, stars, disks, gas regions, obstacles, a magnetic field. The setup uses the keys of a shareable link, as a query string ("problem=sedov&dim=2&n=512&gamma=1.4") or an object ({"problem": "sedov", "dim": 2, "n": 512}). Returns the run’s state, including `query`, the setup in force.

args.name: setup
args.description: Query string, link, or object of setup keys; or a setup document itself

args.name: document
args.description: A setup document (format "shaderous-setup", see docs/setups.md and describe().setup): the run is built from it, and `setup` then says the grid and what differs. Start from preset(id) to make one

api.name: loadAthdf
api.summary: Start a run from an .athdf file: one Shaderous wrote continues exactly; another code’s is loaded into the current problem. Paused at the file’s time.

api.name: state
api.summary: The run: problem, dimensions, grid, amr levels, time, timestep, steps, end time, whether it has finished, the GPU adapter, and `query`, the setup that reproduces it.

api.name: run
api.summary: Advance the run: to time `until` (the last step is shortened to land on it exactly), by `steps` steps, or whichever comes first. Stops at the problem’s end time (stopped: "end"); to go further, load with a later `tend`. Returns t, dt, steps, steps taken, wall seconds and why it stopped.

until.description: Run until the clock reads this time

steps.description: Take at most this many steps

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this much wall time, in milliseconds

api.name: step
api.summary: Take n steps (one, without n).

api.name: runTo
api.summary: Run until the clock reads t, landed on exactly.

api.name: restart
api.summary: Start the run again from its initial conditions, paused.

api.name: play
api.summary: Let the page’s own loop step the run, as the Run button does.

api.name: pause
api.summary: Stop the page’s own loop from stepping the run.

api.name: diagnostics
api.summary: Totals and extremes read back now: mass, momentum, kinetic/internal/gravitational/total energy, max Mach number, floored cells, Jeans-unresolved cells, center of mass, point masses, and the [min, max] of every field.

api.name: debris
api.summary: Debris energies, for problems that track them (describe: problems[].debris, e.g. tidal-disruption): the gas binned by its specific orbital energy about the point mass, both what has left the box (tallied as it left) and what is in it, a surviving self-bound core set apart, and the return rate of the bound debris to pericenter, dM/dt (Kepler).

api.name: impact
api.summary: What a giant impact has left (3D runs with gravity, e.g. moon-forming-impact): the gas sorted by the Kepler orbit each cell is on about the densest body into the planet (pericenter inside it), the disk around it and what escapes, with each part’s mass, the share of it that is each species and the mean dye, the disk’s angular momentum, and the mass of the moon the disk would gather into.

api.name: stats
api.summary: Least, greatest and volume-weighted mean of each variable over the box (rho, press, vel1-3, r0 and species mass fractions).

api.name: slice
api.summary: A variable on a res x res grid on a plane through the box (perpendicular to `axis` at fraction `pos`).

variable.description: One of rho, press, vel1, vel2, vel3, r0, level, temp, tempK, or the name of a species. temp is the temperature in code units, tempK in kelvin (a setup with physical units). Default rho

res.description: Default: the size of the grid, at most 256 (the MCP tool: 32)

encoding.description: json (default): the values as a list; base64: as float32 bytes in `array`, many times faster to bring out of the page at a large res

api.name: probe
api.summary: The gas at points given as fractions of the box ([x, y, z], z ignored in 2D): density, pressure, velocity, passive scalar, temperature (temp in code units; tempK in kelvin, with physical units), refinement level and species mass fractions.

api.name: screenshot
api.summary: A picture of the run as a PNG image.

native.description: One pixel per cell of the finest level (the grid's own resolution, up to the largest texture): true or 'box' for the whole box, 'view' for the part in view. A plane only (a 2D run, a slice or a projection); not with width or height

overlays.description: { colorbar, triad, status }: draw the color bar, the axes and the status line (all off by default)

layout.description: 'over': the overlays over the picture's edges, as in a movie; 'beside': in margins around it, covering nothing. Default 'beside' with native, else 'over'

api.name: record
api.summary: Record the run from where it is as an MP4 movie (H.264), stepping it as it goes: the current view with a color bar, x/y/z axes and the status line (grid, simulation time) over it. A frame every `every` steps, or near every `dt` of code time (at the nearest step boundary: no step is shortened, so the run is the one it would have been unrecorded). Stops at `until`, after `frames` frames, or at the end time. Set the view first.

dt.description: A frame near every multiple of this much code time (default: a 600th of the dynamical time of the problem, so one dynamical time plays in 10 s at 60 fps)

every.description: Or a frame every this many steps

until.description: Stop when the clock reaches this time (landed on exactly)

height.description: Default 1080 (9/16 of width when width is given)

bitrate.description: Bits per second of movie (default 0.2 bits per pixel per frame)

overlays.description: { colorbar, triad, status }, all on by default

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this much wall time, keeping what was recorded

download.description: Hand the file to the browser as a download (default true)

base64.description: Return the file in the result as `base64`

api.name: stopRecording
api.summary: End the recording under way: the file is finished with the frames recorded so far.

api.name: recordingStatus
api.summary: The recording under way, or null.

api.name: view
api.summary: Change what screenshots show without touching the run. Returns the view settings.

args.name: changes
args.description: Any of mode, field, species, log, lo, hi, sliceAxis, slicePos, minRho, opacity, yaw, pitch, dist, tx, ty, tz, zoom, cx, cy, showBlocks, contours, nContours, fog, surfaceOpacity, light, box, fieldLines, fieldLineCount, fieldLineFloor, mirrorImages, turnWithFrame, colormap, tf, autoRange

api.name: athdf
api.summary: The state of the gas as an .athdf file (HDF5 in Athena++’s layout; yt reads it), base64. The file carries the setup, so loading it continues the run exactly.

api.name: athdfChunk
api.summary: Bytes of the .athdf file athdf({ chunked: true }) holds, base64: a file of gigabytes is read out in pieces.

api.name: athdfPut
api.summary: One piece of an .athdf file for loadAthdf() with no argument: its bytes from `offset`, base64, of a file of `total` bytes.

api.name: snapshotOut
api.summary: The state of the gas as a snapshot held in the page, for a caller that writes the .athdf file itself: its fields but the arrays, and each array’s key, type and length. Read the arrays with snapshotChunk, then call snapshotDone.

api.name: snapshotChunk
api.summary: Bytes of an array of the snapshot snapshotOut() holds, base64.

api.name: snapshotDone
api.summary: Let the snapshot snapshotOut() holds go.

api.name: snapshotIn
api.summary: Set out a snapshot for loadSnapshot(): its fields but the arrays, and the arrays’ keys, types and lengths, as snapshotOut gives them.

api.name: snapshotPut
api.summary: One piece of an array of the snapshot snapshotIn() set out: its bytes from `offset`, base64.

api.name: loadSnapshot
api.summary: Start a run from the snapshot snapshotIn() and snapshotPut() put together, as loadAthdf does from a file. Paused at its time.

api.name: controls
api.summary: The control panel as it stands: every control’s id, kind, label, tooltip, value and options. Use with `control` to change settings mid-run.

api.name: control
api.summary: Set a panel control (or press a button, with no value) exactly as a person would, mid-run, and wait for what it starts (a shader rebuild, a restart). Examples: control("riemann", "hll"), control("eos", "gas_radiation"), control("reset"). Number fields take values in the units the panel shows; set control("units", "code") first for code units. The run stays paused.

api.name: tool
api.summary: Use one of the editing tools, as a person would with the pointer, applied now between steps and logged: mass (add or remove gas), velocity, temperature, obstacle (a shape in a plane of the box, cut through it along the plane normal), field (make the magnetic field stronger or weaker), pull (drag the field lines from one point to another), source, sink, star (3D), clear (the sources or the sinks), or query (the gas at a point). Positions are fractions of the box ([x, y] or [x, y, z]), velocities code units; the rest as the tool’s sliders take them. Unknown options are an error.

pos.description: Center, in fractions of the box (z defaults to the middle)

radius.description: Brush radius, or the radius of a source, sink or star, as a fraction of the box

softness.description: Brush edge: 0 hard, 1 fading all the way from the center

amount.description: mass: density added at the center as a share of the densest gas (negative removes; default 0.25)

atRest.description: mass: new gas arrives at rest, sharing the momentum there (default true)

vel.description: velocity: the velocity to set; source, sink, star: its velocity (code units)

factor.description: temperature, field: the factor applied at the center (default 1.5; below 1 lowers it)

center.description: obstacle: rect or ellipse center, in the plane’s two coordinates

axis.description: obstacle: the plane’s normal, along which it is cut through the box (default 2, z; its coordinates are then x and y, for 0 y and z, for 1 x and z)

erase.description: obstacle: turn obstacle back into gas

to.description: pull: where it ends (taken frame by frame, as the tool would)

grip.description: pull: the share of the drag the field at the center moves by (default 0.5)

mass.description: sink: its mass as a multiple of the gas in the box (default 0: a massless particle)

soften.description: sink: softening length of its gravity, as a fraction of the box

fixed.description: source, sink: held where it is placed (default false)

beta.description: star: plasma beta at its center

api.name: actions
api.summary: The session log of the run: the setup it started from, and every edit since (the tools, settings changed, the adaptive mesh’s re-meshes), each with the step it was applied at, with the run’s diagnostics along the way. The page’s Save session log button saves the same.

api.name: replay
api.summary: Run a session log again: load the setup it started from, step to each action and apply it, re-meshing where it re-meshed, so the run comes out as it did (to the bit, on the same machine). Returns how many actions it applied, and where it stopped if the run went another way.

args.name: log
args.description: A session log, as actions() returns it

untilSteps.description: Stop at this many steps (default: after the last action)

api.name: errors
api.summary: What the page has reported going wrong (uncaught errors, failed shader builds, a lost GPU device), oldest first.

tools.name: edit
tools.brief: Uses an editing tool on the run, as a person would: `name` (mass, velocity, temperature, obstacle, field, pull, source, sink, star, clear, query) and its `options`
tools.description: Use one of the editing tools, as a person would with the pointer, applied now between steps and logged: mass (add or remove gas), velocity, temperature, obstacle (a shape in a plane of the box, cut through it along the plane normal), field (make the magnetic field stronger or weaker), pull (drag the field lines from one point to another), source, sink, star (3D), clear (the sources or the sinks), or query (the gas at a point). Positions are fractions of the box ([x, y] or [x, y, z]), velocities code units; the rest as the tool’s sliders take them. Unknown options are an error.

pos.description: Center, in fractions of the box (z defaults to the middle)

radius.description: Brush radius, or the radius of a source, sink or star, as a fraction of the box

softness.description: Brush edge: 0 hard, 1 fading all the way from the center

amount.description: mass: density added at the center as a share of the densest gas (negative removes; default 0.25)

atRest.description: mass: new gas arrives at rest, sharing the momentum there (default true)

vel.description: velocity: the velocity to set; source, sink, star: its velocity (code units)

factor.description: temperature, field: the factor applied at the center (default 1.5; below 1 lowers it)

center.description: obstacle: rect or ellipse center, in the plane’s two coordinates

axis.description: obstacle: the plane’s normal, along which it is cut through the box (default 2, z; its coordinates are then x and y, for 0 y and z, for 1 x and z)

erase.description: obstacle: turn obstacle back into gas

to.description: pull: where it ends (taken frame by frame, as the tool would)

grip.description: pull: the share of the drag the field at the center moves by (default 0.5)

mass.description: sink: its mass as a multiple of the gas in the box (default 0: a massless particle)

soften.description: sink: softening length of its gravity, as a fraction of the box

fixed.description: source, sink: held where it is placed (default false)

beta.description: star: plasma beta at its center

tools.name: session_log
tools.brief: Summarizes what has been done to the run since it started (actions by kind, steps), and writes the full session log to `save_path`
tools.description: The session log of the run: the setup it started from, and every edit since (the tools, settings changed, the adaptive mesh’s re-meshes), each with the step it was applied at, with the run’s diagnostics along the way. The page’s Save session log button saves the same. Returns a summary: the setup, whether it can be replayed, the actions by kind and the steps they span. save_path writes the full log as JSON, for replay.

save_path.description: Write the session log as JSON to this file

tools.name: replay
tools.brief: Runs a saved session log (a file written by session_log or the page’s Save session log button) again, step for step
tools.description: Run a session log again: load the setup it started from, step to each action and apply it, re-meshing where it re-meshed, so the run comes out as it did (to the bit, on the same machine). Returns how many actions it applied, and where it stopped if the run went another way.

untilSteps.description: Stop at this many steps (default: after the last action)

tools.name: errors
tools.brief: Lists what the page has reported going wrong
tools.description: What the page has reported going wrong (uncaught errors, failed shader builds, a lost GPU device), oldest first.
